title: Stop Student Debt Relief Scams Act of 2019
official_summary:
Stop Student Debt Relief Scams Act of 2019

This bill establishes criminal penalties for unauthorized access of certain student loan information and expands the requirements for student loan exit counseling.

Specifically, the bill makes it a crime to knowingly use an access device (e.g., account number) that was issued to another person or was fraudulently obtained to access Department of Education (ED) information technology systems for commercial advantage or private financial gain. A violator is subject to criminal penalties—a fine, a prison term of up to five years, or both.

Further, the bill expands loan exit counseling requirements to require an institution of higher education that participates in federal student-aid programs to provide an explanation to borrowers cautioning them about third-party student debt relief companies.

It also requires ED to prevent unauthorized access to the central database for student aid (i.e., the National Student Loan Data System) and warn borrowers of suspicious activity regarding their student loan accounts.

summary.headline: A 2020 federal law makes it a crime to misuse someone else's student loan account access for profit and adds scam warnings to student loan exit counseling.
summary.what_it_does: The law makes it a federal crime to knowingly use an account number or other access device that belongs to someone else, or was obtained fraudulently, to get into Department of Education systems for personal financial gain. A person convicted can face a fine, up to five years in prison, or both. It also requires colleges that take part in federal student aid to warn borrowers during exit counseling about third-party debt relief companies. The Department of Education must work to block unauthorized access to the National Student Loan Data System and warn borrowers about suspicious activity on their loan accounts.

who_it_affects.how: They are warned about third-party debt relief companies and told to watch for suspicious activity on their loan accounts.

who_it_affects.group: People who misuse others' student loan account access
who_it_affects.how: Using someone else's access device to get into Department of Education systems for profit is now a federal crime with possible prison time and fines.

who_it_affects.group: Colleges and universities that participate in federal student aid programs
who_it_affects.how: They must include a caution about third-party student debt relief companies in the exit counseling they give departing borrowers.
They are now the subject of required federal warnings given to borrowers at exit counseling.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 22, 2020; specific provisions take effect on the date of enactment unless otherwise stated in the statute.
